title: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
summary: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month s Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe , Apple , Google  and Mozilla .
card_summary: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month s Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws including a zero-day in…

sections.overview: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month s Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe , Apple , Google  and Mozilla .
sections.technical:
According to Redmond, just one of the flaws is already seeing active exploitation: CVE-2026-124194 , a spoofing bug in Outlook. Nearly half of those critical bugs are remote code execution vulnerabilities. Google this week released Chrome version 157.0.8103.50 , which resolves nine security holes, including  CVE-2026-125350 , the sixth zero-day vulnerability this year for Chrome (this bug also being patched in Chromium-based browsers like Edge). November s patch release from Redmond tackles 1,093 vulnerabilities, fixing 63 critical flaws that can be exploited to seize control over a Windows system with little or no help from users.

Referenced vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-124194, CVE-2026-125350.
sections.impact:
The advisory for CVE-2026-124194 says it affects Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise and editions of Microsoft Office . November s patch release from Redmond tackles 1,093 vulnerabilities, fixing 63 critical flaws that can be exploited to seize control over a Windows system with little or no help from users. Chris Goettl , vice president of product management at Ivanti , said it s easy for security teams at large enterprises to feel overwhelmed by the volume and criticality of patches from Microsoft lately.

Assessed severity: CRITICAL.
sections.context: This story is part of the recurring zero-day pattern where exploitation pressure is highest before broad patch adoption.

email_summary: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. Tracked as CVE-2026-124194, CVE-2026-125350. Severity is rated critical.
